correctness.rationale: The tridiagonal row-stochastic 4x4 recurrence J has positive irreducible off-diagonals, a simple real spectrum and orthogonal polynomials R_i normalized at one; coefficients g(m,n;k)=[R_m(J)]_{n,k}. All R1 multiplications are nonnegative, so only (2,2),(2,3),(3,3) must be checked. Independent symbolic SymPy reconstruction of R2(J),R3(J) verified the source 12 exact coefficient formulas and their row sums: only L/(1-x), H/(1-x), rH/[(1-x)(1-y)] and (1-r)K/(1-y) can be negative for 0<r<1. At r=1, K disappears, H=1-x-y and H>=0 forces L=1-x(1+y)>0. For every ratio r, H(r=1)>=0 forces x+y<=1 and limit K(r->1-) enforces y<=2/3; these two conditions force H,K>=0 and L>0 by the stated y(2-3y) bound. Independent exact rational witnesses verify L independence and a profile with negative third Newton coefficient. This is an all-real-parameter symbolic proof, not a finite parameter sampling claim.

final_claim: For four-point finite orthogonal polynomial systems with 0<x<y<1 and constant downward-to-total ratio 0<r<=1, nonnegative product linearization is equivalent to H>=0,K>=0,L>=0 for 0<r<1, to x+y<=1 at r=1, and holds for every 0<r<=1 precisely if x+y<=1 and y<=2/3.
limitations: Exactly four spectral points and profiles 0<x<y<1 with one constant ratio r; endpoint r=1 separate from interior criterion.
residual_risks: Older specialized four-point polynomial hypergroup tables may encode the same profile boundaries
